analysis.title: The Day Ahead - North America, Monday October 26, 2026
key_insights: Wall Street closed lower on Monday. The Dow fell 1.23% to 52,215.16, the S&P 500 lost 0.52% to 7,623.68 and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.21% to 25,955.34. For the week the S&P 500 fell 0.47%, the Nasdaq declined 0.71% and the Dow rose 0.41%.

Doubts about the durability of the AI-stock rally continue to weigh on equities. Man Group's Kristina Hooper said there is potential for less AI data center build-out spending next year than projected. About one-third of the S&P 500 reports next, including Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, whose capex forecasts are the focus.
The Fed's two-day meeting starts Tuesday and the decision is due Wednesday at 14:00 ET. The funds rate is expected to stay at 3.75%-4.00%, followed by a press conference from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.

Treasury yields rose after the 10-year's biggest one-day drop in nearly four years. The 10-year yielded 4.9986%, the 2-year 4.6839% and the 30-year 5.3264%. BondBloxx's JoAnne Bianco expects the 10-year back above 5% on sticky inflation, heavier Treasury supply to fund deficits, higher term premiums and elevated energy prices.

Oil rose on Houthi attacks across Saudi Arabia, including on energy infrastructure. Brent gained 3.51% to $117.14 and WTI rose 4.18% to $103.63. A tanker oil spill off the UAE coast was also reported.

Gold fell 0.67% to $3,996.83 as higher energy prices raised inflation concerns and reinforced US rate hike expectations. Margin calls from the tech selloff also pushed some investors to sell gold and silver, per American Gold Exchange's Jim Wyckoff.

The euro fell as a French government bond selloff pushed France's risk premium to its highest since 2011. Moody's reviews France's rating on Friday. The euro lost 0.19% to $1.1193 and the dollar index fell 0.19% to 101.80.

Thursday carries the heaviest US data load: Q3 advance GDP (expected 3.2% annualized vs 2.2%), September PCE inflation (core expected +0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y, headline +0.5% m/m and 3.6% y/y) and personal income and spending. Weekly jobless claims also come out Thursday.

Tuesday US data includes October consumer confidence (expected 83.5 vs 81.9), September durable goods (text cites +1.2% expected, the calendar table cites a 0.6% poll) and new home sales (645,000 expected in the text, 0.66 million in the calendar table, vs 684,000 prior).

The big-tech earnings slate: Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday, Amazon and Intel report Thursday after the close (Intel date given as Thursday). Apple is expected to show new MacBooks Wednesday, possibly its first touch-screen laptop. Apple's $2,000 foldable iPhone Duo launched with rationed supply.

Other key earnings this week: Boeing, UPS, HCA, Centene, PayPal, Coca-Cola and Freeport-McMoRan on Tuesday. FedEx, Chipotle, Phillips 66, HF Sinclair, Biogen and Smithfield on Wednesday. Eli Lilly, Merck, Bristol Myers, Caterpillar, Ares, Blue Owl, Cheniere, Starbucks, Restaurant Brands and Altria on Thursday. AbbVie and Chevron on Friday, with Exxon filing Friday.

Monday after-close reports include Cadence, Nucor, Public Storage, Welltower, Cincinnati Financial, Principal Financial, Brown & Brown and Alexandria Real Estate, with The Hartford at 16:05 ET. Verizon reported at 07:00 ET.

SLB beat third-quarter profit estimates on North American oilfield demand and signaled a stronger 2027 as Middle East activity recovers. Halliburton also forecast mid-single-digit revenue growth in 2027. SLB rose 7.25% to $53.14.

American Express raised its 2026 profit forecast above expectations and will cut 5% of its workforce, about 3,500 jobs. Third-quarter expenses were $14.5 billion, up 9% y/y. Barclays also cited AI-driven efficiency for layoffs.
S&P 500 movers: Crown Castle +9.21%, CrowdStrike +7.89%, SLB +7.25%. Decliners were Comfort Systems USA -9.55%, Globe Life -8.22% and AT&T -7.61%.

Flash US Composite PMI slipped to 57.6 in October from a five-year high of 58.4. New orders rose to 58.2, the highest since March 2022, and the output prices gauge rose to 59.8, the highest since August 2022. S&P Global flagged precautionary stock building.
US consumer sentiment is near a record low in October as Middle East conflict-driven price rises sour households ahead of midterm elections on November 3.
Hedge funds posted their worst day since the COVID-era rout in major strategies amid the tech selloff this week.

Bank of Canada is expected to raise its rate 25bp to 2.50% on October 28 and hike once more by end-March, per a Reuters poll. The TSX fell 0.52% to 35,788.18 while energy was the only sector to gain, up 2.05%.

Airlines are cutting capacity discipline into fuel costs: jet fuel is up roughly 90% since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in February, squeezing profits and forcing forecast cuts. More industry capacity in 2027 may make this year's fare gains harder to repeat.

Six more companies including Wells Fargo, Arm and Intuit objected to tokenization of their shares on the OKX and ICE joint platform. That brings total objections to 22, including Microsoft and Alphabet, despite SEC approval of the products.

SK Hynix put the US IPO of its Solidigm chip unit on hold on market volatility and South Korean regulator concerns. Meta delayed new commercial terms to November 20 after publisher and advertiser complaints in the EU and UK.
earnings_insights: SLB Q3: beat Wall Street profit estimates (estimate figure not given in the note). Middle East and Asia revenue was $2.81 billion, up 9% sequentially and down 6% y/y. The Middle East was 34% of total 2025 revenue.
American Express Q3 reported: consolidated expenses $14.5 billion, up 9% y/y. 2026 profit forecast raised above Street expectations (figures not given).
Chevron Q3 (reports Friday): EPS expected up 62% y/y per LSEG data, a consensus estimate and not yet printed.
Cheniere Q3 (reports Thursday): adjusted EPS estimate $4.07 and net income estimate $846.99 million, both consensus and not yet printed.

Monday after-close consensus per LSEG Smart Estimates (not yet reported): Cadence EPS $2.05 on revenue $1,612.94 million, Nucor EPS $5.79 vs $5.92 IBES EPS estimate on revenue $10,834.37 million, Cincinnati Financial $2.19 vs $1.99, Public Storage $2.23 vs $2.39, Welltower $0.69 vs $0.66, Principal Financial $2.42, Brown & Brown $1.08, The Hartford $3.20, Alexandria Real Estate -$0.03. Verizon estimate $1.27 on revenue $34,744.03 million.
Phillips 66 and HF Sinclair are expected to report higher adjusted Q3 earnings y/y on stronger refining margins from Middle East tensions boosting US fuel exports (estimates not given).
Coca-Cola, Chipotle and Restaurant Brands are expected to post higher Q3 revenue, Starbucks a fourth-quarter revenue decline and Smithfield a drop in Q3 sales (all expectations, not yet reported).
Caterpillar's construction and power & energy units have benefited from AI data center demand. Eli Lilly's focus is diabetes and weight-loss medicine sales and any change to full-year outlook.

Boeing enters Q3 with F/A-XX contract wins and 737 MAX 7 and 10 certification but production challenges on the 737 and 787. UPS is shifting toward higher-margin international air shipments as it delivers millions fewer Amazon packages.

crypto_views: Six more companies, including Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit, will not allow their shares to be tokenized on the OKX and Intercontinental Exchange joint platform. 22 companies have objected in total, 16 of them Nasdaq-listed including Microsoft and Alphabet.
The SEC recently approved tokenized stock products, and its exam priorities include AI, private assets and tokenized securities.
risk_factors: Reduced AI data center capex next year versus current projections, which hyperscaler earnings this week could confirm.
Sticky inflation with energy prices expected to stay high, plus heavier Treasury supply and higher term premiums that could push the 10-year back above 5%.
Middle East supply disruption from the Houthi attacks and the Iran war.
French sovereign risk and the Moody's review on Friday.
AI-discovered software vulnerabilities that cyber experts say will likely trigger more outages like those hitting global government websites this week.
Consumer strain from higher mortgage costs and energy costs, with sentiment near a record low.
Airline capacity growth in 2027 combined with high fuel costs.
vol_and_positioning: Global hedge funds had major strategies post their worst day since the COVID-era market rout this week amid the tech selloff.
The tech selloff has caused margin calls for equity traders and investors, prompting sales of gold and silver, per Jim Wyckoff of American Gold Exchange.
geopolitical: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels carried out attacks across Saudi Arabia including on energy infrastructure, lifting oil prices.
The US-Israeli war on Iran began in February and has raised jet fuel prices roughly 90%.

French government bond selloff pushed France's risk premium to its highest since 2011. Moody's reviews France's rating Friday and the Macron government has threatened military assistance to quell social unrest.
UAE authorities reported an oil spill from a tanker off Umm Al Quwain.

US-Canada trade talks collapsed in August. Carney says there is no merit to US claims of Canadian interference in the November 3 midterms and Canada is in no rush for a deal. The US is expected to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products.
Middle East activity is expected to recover in 2027 per SLB and Halliburton if conflict-related disruption resolves.
South Korean authorities raised concerns over SK Hynix's planned US listing of Solidigm.
Canada and Turkey upgraded relations to a strategic partnership, and AtkinsRealis is in the running for Turkey's second nuclear plant.

tension_points.bull_case: Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon earnings could fuel the next leg of the AI rally, with demand for data centers supporting Caterpillar's power unit and AI infrastructure financing at Blue Owl and Ares.
tension_points.bear_case: Man Group's Kristina Hooper says less may be invested in AI data center build-out next year than projected. Sell-offs in AI-related stocks and jitters over the sustainability of the AI investment boom have put the spotlight on risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler capital spending forecasts for next year coming in below current projections would break the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: The 10-year saw its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years and remains under 5%.
tension_points.bear_case: BondBloxx's JoAnne Bianco expects yields over 5% again on sticky inflation, growing Treasury supply to finance deficits, higher term premiums and persistent higher energy prices.
